transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (HorizonLedger Lead ML Eng), Marcus Chen (Platform), Priya Rao (Security)

Summary:
Quick demo/walkthrough of Redwood SDK starter kit (Python + TypeScript), authentication patterns (API key, GCP Workload Identity), console walkthrough for model selection, and a short tour of Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization. Customer wants a sandbox/proof-of-concept to validate latency/cost for their transaction-parsing pipeline.

Topics covered:
- SDK quickstart (env vars, installing, example call)
- Auth options: API key vs Workload Identity vs private deployment considerations
- Console: model catalog, routing and rollouts, cost insights
- Optimize: batching, prefix cache, quantization suggestions and tradeoffs
- Next steps and action items

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Ava with Redwood and with me is Samir our solutions engineer. Quick check, can you hear us okay?
[00:06] Lena: Yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:08] Marcus: Good here.
[00:10] Ava: Great. Agenda for the next hour is a hands-on look at the StarterKit repo, cover auth options, spin up a sandbox API key and then show Optimize suggestions that might map to your transaction parsing workload. If anything is off schedule call it out.
[00:25] Samir: I'll start with the Python quickstart, then show the TypeScript snippet and how the console ties into the same token. Note: in the repo we included both dotenv and workload identity examples.
[00:35] Lena: Perfect, we're primarily Python but have a couple Node services for webhooks. Also Priya is here for security questions.
[00:44] Priya: Thanks, quick note — we can't store raw PII in third-party logs and we'll need KMS integration for key rotation.
[00:51] Ava: Absolutely understood. We'll show the K-M-S flow and our audit logs. Samir, go ahead.
[00:58] Samir: Alright, repo live in the screen share now. File structure: /python, /ts, /infra-examples. In python/README we have pip install redwood-client, env var REDWOOD_API_KEY for simple flow. Example call: client.generate(prompt=...) returns a streaming generator.
[01:20] Samir: Note: the client does automatic retry and backoff by default, which is handy for noisy connections. There is a small example for continuous batching in the utils.
[01:33] Marcus: When you say batching is automatic, is that on our side or server side? Do we need to change anything in our code?
[01:40] Samir: Good question — Redwood does server-side batching but the client hints (max_concurrent_requests, affinity key) can be used to help the runtime batch similar requests. The quickstart includes recommended defaults.
[01:54] Lena: What's the default tokenization model? Like, how do we get embeddings vs chat?
[01:59] Samir: The SDK exposes endpoints: text.generate, chat.create, embeddings.create. Model selection is passed as model="redwood-rl-1" or a model id from the console. The console shows cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[02:13] Priya: Can you show the console — specifically where audit logs and retention settings live?
[02:17] Ava: Sure. Switching to the Console. Top nav: Projects -> Models -> Observability. Here we can set retention, and under Security there is KMS key binding and SSO config.
[02:29] Samir: There's also an option to route requests to Dedicated pool vs Hosted to control data residency. In Private mode you get a customer-controlled control plane and audit logs that don't leave your VPC.
[02:42] Priya: Is the Private deployment an on-prem bundle or VPC-hosted? What's the difference for our compliance needs?
[02:48] Ava: We offer both: VPC-hosted for cloud projects where you want the control plane in your account, and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. For SOC2 auditing we provide detailed logs and can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:02] Marcus: For the workload identity, do we need any daemon running or can we use workload identity federation with GCP?
[03:09] Samir: You can use GCP workload identity federation. In the TS example we show how to exchange a GCP short-lived token for a Redwood token via our token exchange endpoint — avoids long-lived secrets.
[03:22] Samir: Showing code: const client = new RedwoodClient({auth: {gcpWorkload: true, projectId: 'horizon-ledger-dev'}}) — that snippet calls fetch() to our token exchange URL and caches the short-lived token.
[03:36] Lena: That helps. Are there RBAC roles for service accounts? We want least privilege.
[03:41] Ava: Yes, you can assign roles at project and route level — e.g., generate-only, admin, read-only. We usually recommend a service account with generate-only for inference traffic.
[03:52] Priya: About KMS, can Redwood wrap customer keys so keys are never sent to you?
[03:58] Samir: We support envelope encryption — you can bring your own key (BYOK) through KMS/HSM integration. The Redwood service never stores the unwrapped key in plaintext; only a wrapped key reference is held.
[04:13] Marcus: Great. Now the Optimize piece — what metrics does it use to recommend batching and quantization?
[04:20] Samir: Optimize analyzes token distribution, latency SLOs, and cost per token. It suggests batching window sizes and quantization profile (int8 vs int4) and shows estimated cost savings and expected latency impact.
[04:33] Samir: Example: for short prompts (avg 30 tokens) it recommended a 25ms batching window which yields 18% cost reduction with a median latency increase of ~10ms.
[04:45] Lena: We have transaction messages that vary a lot; will prefix caching help?
[04:50] Samir: Yes if there's common prefix text in your prompts (like instruction templates) prefix/K-V cache can avoid recomputing early layers. In our console Optimize shows prefix hit rate projections.
[05:02] Marcus: Any concerns with quantization and output quality? We can't have hallucinations on financial intents.
[05:08] Samir: Absolutely — Optimize ties recommendations to eval sets. You can upload a representative prompt set and it runs lightweight evals to estimate regression risk. We flagged any model-quantization pairs that failed quality thresholds.
[05:21] Priya: How do we run those evals? Is that in the console or CLI?
[05:25] Samir: Both — console has an Eval runner UI, and the CLI/SDK has an eval.run() that will return metrics. We provide a template with metrics we recommend for financial workloads.
[05:36] Lena: Let's try a short live test — can you generate from the sandbox key you mentioned?
[05:40] Ava: Sure — I'll create a sandbox API key scoped to the dev project and send it in the chat. It will be time-limited and restricted to the sandbox CIDR.
[05:52] Ava: (typing) Created. Key id: sk-test-hz-... I'm pasting the link to the quickstart repo and the key instructions.
[06:00] Marcus: Got the link. We'll use workload identity for the Node webhook and API key for local dev.
[06:06] Samir: Walkthrough: in python/.env set REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-hz-... then run python examples/generate.py. The example shows streaming via SSE and writes partial chunks to stdout.
[06:20] (short cough)
[06:22] Lena: I'm seeing a snippet that calls client.create_chat, is the conversation state persisted by us or Redwood?
[06:28] Samir: By default, conversation state isn't persisted — you pass in the messages you want to keep. If you opt into server-side history features there's explicit toggles and retention controls. We don't persist by default without consent.
[06:42] Priya: Are the logs encrypted at rest and in transit? We need proof for intake.
[06:46] Ava: Yes TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. We'll include the crypto whitepaper in the security pack.
[06:58] Marcus: On the topic of routing — can we set a policy to send high priority requests to dedicated pool and low priority to hosted to save cost?
[07:05] Samir: Yes that's the smart routing policy. You can set priority flags on requests or routes and the runtime will prefer dedicated if available, otherwise fall back to hosted. Policies are configurable by percentage or latency threshold.
[07:19] Lena: For the quickstart repo, does the TypeScript example include a short-lived token flow for Vercel?
[07:24] Samir: Yes, ts/examples/vercel-auth shows how to use serverless functions to mint a short-lived token via the token exchange endpoint and then call the Redwood API from the browser with that token.
[07:36] Priya: We also need audit events for who rotated keys and when. Does Redwood provide immutable audit trails?
[07:42] Ava: We do. Audit events are exported to your SIEM via webhook or pushed to your S3. They include user, action, IP, and resource.
[07:53] Marcus: Can we run a small perf benchmark for our pipeline? We want p50, p95 latency at 512 tokens.
[07:59] Samir: We can — Samir: I can run a quick client-side benchmark from the sandbox endpoint now to show rough numbers, or we can run a more controlled benchmark with our infra team. Which do you prefer?
[08:10] Lena: Rough numbers now are fine to get a feel.
[08:12] Samir: Running bench (simulated 20 concurrent clients, 512 tokens, model redwood-std-2) ... p50 ~ 82ms, p95 ~ 240ms in the hosted sandbox. Note: your production numbers will vary by routing and dedicated capacity.
[08:28] Lena: That baseline is useful. Any recommended next steps for us to evaluate cost?
[08:33] Samir: Upload a representative workload trace and we can run Optimize with that dataset to give a cost projection and recommended quantization/batching profile.
[08:42] Priya: On legal side, we'll need a DPA and data processing terms before we move PII in.
[08:48] Ava: Understood, legal will share the standard DPA and we can scope out amendments for additional clauses.
[08:55] Marcus: What about tokenization differences — are embeddings and generation token units the same billing unit?
[09:01] Samir: Embeddings are billed per 1k vector units and generation per token. The console shows a breakdown and the SDK returns token usage per call.
[09:12] Lena: Anything else on the repo?
[09:14] Samir: We included CI examples for rotating secrets in GitHub Actions and a small terraform module for provisioning a sandbox VPC and IAM roles.
[09:24] Marcus: Let's talk timeline — we want a POC by end of the month if possible. What do you need from us?
[09:30] Ava: To kick off a 3-week POC we'd need your sandbox project and VPC CIDR, a small prompt corpus (1k samples) for evals, and the stakeholders for a weekly check-in. We'll prepare an onboarding doc and sample test harness.
[09:46] Lena: We can do that.
[09:48] Priya: One more question: is there a way to keep inference logs inside our account so Redwood never sees payloads?
[09:54] Samir: In Private deployment yes. For hosted we support request-level encryption and selective logging. Also you can enable on-prem routing for ultra-sensitive flows.
[10:06] Ava: Ok wrapping up, I'll repeat the next steps in chat and send the security pack. Samir will create the quickstart repo variant with the workload identity example for your GCP setup. Marcus you'll share VPC details.
[10:19] Lena: Thanks both, this was super helpful.
[10:22] Marcus: Appreciate it.
[10:24] Priya: Thanks.
[10:26] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set a POC kickoff.

End of transcript.

References shared in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starterkit-pipeline , Security pack (link sent in follow-up), Sandbox key (via secure note in chat).
